title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
event_hint: Systematic evaluation of programmatic vs JSON tool calling across 14 LLMs on BFCL v4 benchmark
problem: Lack of systematic evaluation comparing programmatic tool calling (tools as code) to native JSON tool calling across model generations under real-world task conditions
mechanism: Programmatic tool calling exposes tools as typed Python stubs that models invoke through executable code, with execution and results handled in a single agent turn via subprocess, replacing rigid JSON function-call objects

evidence.claim: 11 of 14 models match or exceed baseline accuracy under programmatic tool calling on BFCL v4 subset
GPT-5.6 family achieves 10.6% absolute improvement over JSON tool calling baseline
Programmatic tool calling achieves 18.8% absolute accuracy gap over JSON tool calling at chain lengths ≥12
evidence.condition: Sequential chaining tasks, 52 entries, chain lengths 2-20

evidence.claim: JSON tool calling drops tool calls above model-specific fan-out threshold (N=70-72 for Claude Sonnet 5); programmatic maintains 100% at N=100
evidence.baseline: JSON tool calling drops calls at N=70-72
evidence.condition: Claude Sonnet 5, parallel fan-out with probe entries at N∈{60,70,72,75,100}

evidence.claim: Under context flooding, programmatic tool calling stable (+5.5%), JSON degrades 2.3%, filesystem-discovery degrades 32%
evidence.condition: Context rot ablation, 31 entries per condition, 128 total schemas (flood vs filtered)

evaluation_context: 309-entry BFCL v4 subset across 8 task categories (simple_python, multiple, parallel, parallel_multiple, live_simple, live_multiple, live_parallel, live_parallel_multiple). 14 models evaluated spanning Anthropic (5 models) and OpenAI (9 models) from November 2024 to July 2026. All experiments at temperature 0. Ablation studies: chaining (n=52, chain lengths 2-20), parallelism (n=32 enumeration entries, fan-out 7-48 plus probes), context rot (n=31 per condition). Deterministic scorer with normalized string comparison. 95% Wilson confidence intervals reported. Per-category accuracy now available (Table 6) showing macro-averaged results across all 14 models.
limitations: Results divide along model generation lines: all Anthropic models and three newest GPT generations match/exceed baseline, while three older GPT models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, GPT-5.4-mini) do not. Small ablation sample sizes (n=31-52) produce wide confidence intervals; only cross-model aggregate patterns treated as reliable. Evaluation limited to representative BFCL v4 subset, not full benchmark. Three OpenAI models exhibit catastrophic \n encoding failures in programmatic tool calling, particularly harmful in chaining and parallel tasks requiring multiline scripts or asyncio.gather. Token consumption evidence limited to single crossover point (N≈26); full cost curves not reported. End-to-end latency not measured. Models frequently produce correct aggregation answers from parametric knowledge without executing enumeration calls, complicating fidelity assessment. Production deployment costs and error recovery not evaluated.
project_relevance: Directly relevant to Agent工具执行链优化. Programmatic tool calling addresses the topic's core question about whether tool calling parallelization introduces correctness risks by demonstrating it matches or exceeds JSON baseline in 13/14 models under fan-out conditions with near-perfect enumeration accuracy. The mechanism (single-turn code execution vs multi-turn JSON calls) may reduce redundant reads and context-building overhead in code agents, but the paper provides minimal empirical data on Read/Grep/tool call counts, token consumption curves, or end-to-end latency—key metrics in the project context. The \n encoding failure mode in older OpenAI models represents a production risk for code agents relying on multiline scripts.

evidence_gaps.question: What are the token consumption and latency differences between programmatic and JSON tool calling paradigms?
What are the error rates and failure modes (syntax errors, runtime errors, hallucinated functions) for programmatic tool calling?
